category_title: Autistic students who partially process problems with discrepancy gestures and echolalia
minimal_context: Rico is working on a task sheet to identify and mark images of concrete objects shaped like a beam and a ball.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please look at this task sheet. Find the images shaped like a beam and a ball, and put a checkmark next to them.

STUDENT: (Focuses on the objects with irregular hand movements. He moves his hand as if about to put a checkmark on the pencil and cap, but hesitates and turns his attention to the tissue box) Tissue... tissue...

TUTOR: Keep looking at the pictures. Which one is the beam?

STUDENT: (His view slowly turns, observing the variety of objects. He makes a discrepancy gesture, pointing his finger at the image of the cap while looking at the beam)

TUTOR: What about the ball? Can you find the ball?

STUDENT: (He ignores the image of the marbles. His hand movements give a checkmark on the picture of the hat instead. He stares at the canned milk and repeats quickly) Canned milk, canned milk.

options.A: Alter how the tutor interprets the given behavior during the task sheet activity, viewing it as a desire for social interaction rather than noncompliance.
options.B: Set a standard of interacting with the student at a ratio of four positive interactions to one negative interaction during the task sheet activity.
options.C: Maintain a quiet and relaxing environment during the task sheet activity by talking gently and slowly, and avoiding loud speech.
options.D: Introduce geometric shapes using concrete objects (e.g., blocks, balls) and establish similarities with the images on the task sheet before proceeding.
